_about: On this day in Essex. A fixed calendar, keyed MM-DD, written once and checked against the source linked on each entry. The newsroom never edits this file. Where a day has more than one entry, the site shows a different one each year.

11-02.t: Anne Knight was born in Chelmsford. The Quaker campaigner fought against slavery and wrote what is thought to be the first leaflet calling for votes for women, in 1847.

11-05.t: BBC Essex went on air for the first time, launching on Bonfire Night.

11-08.t: Martin Peters was born in Plaistow, then part of Essex. He grew up in Dagenham and scored England's second goal in the 1966 World Cup final.

11-09.t: The Seax launched, bringing Essex news, sport and life together in one place. You're reading it.

11-10.t: Edward Bright, the grocer remembered as the Fat Man of Maldon, died aged 29. At more than 40 stone he was thought to be the largest man in England.

11-11.t: News of the Armistice spread across Essex. Towns were soon covered in flags and bunting, and in Braintree work stopped as the celebrations began.
The Mayflower, captained by Harwich mariner Christopher Jones, dropped anchor off Cape Cod after 66 days crossing the Atlantic.

11-18.t: The Dartford Tunnel opened at midday, linking Purfleet with Kent under the Thames. The £13 million tunnel was expected to carry about two million vehicles a year.

11-22.t: Defenders on Southend Pier saw off a 90-minute German air raid, in the first months of the Second World War.

11-23.t: A Thames Conservancy ship broke free of its moorings and smashed a large hole through Southend Pier.

11-24.t: Southend United beat Golders Green 10-1 in the FA Cup first round, one of the biggest wins in the club's history.

11-25.t: Dagenham-born Alf Ramsey scored England's last goal, a penalty, as Hungary won 6-3 at Wembley. Thirteen years later he managed England to World Cup glory.

11-27.t: Saffron Walden-born Henry Winstanley died when the Great Storm swept away the Eddystone Lighthouse he had built. He had gone out to the rock to make repairs.
A record crowd of 19,072 packed Layer Road for Colchester United's FA Cup tie with Reading, only for thick fog to stop the game.

11-29.t: John Ray, the village blacksmith's son who became one of the fathers of natural history, was born in Black Notley near Braintree.
A gale and a spring tide combined to break sea walls along the Essex coast, flooding marshes from St Osyth to Southend's Lower Town.

11-30.t: William Gilbert of Colchester died. Physician to Elizabeth I, his book De Magnete made him a founder of the science of magnetism. He is buried in Holy Trinity Church, Colchester.
